name: Espressif
description: Xtensa architectures for the ESP8266, ESP32, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3, and firmware, ELF, ROM and SVD support for those and the RISC-V ESP32-C2, C3, C5, C6 and H2
longdescription:
Support for Espressif's chips: Xtensa architectures for the ESP8266, ESP32, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3, and firmware loading for those and the RISC-V ESP32-C2, C3, C5, C6 and H2.

- Disassembly in GNU objdump syntax and lifting of the whole Xtensa ISA, with the windowed and call0 calling conventions.
- Firmware images, flash dumps (opened as a container of partitions) and ELF files, mapped into the chip's memory.
- Mask ROM function names and types, and, with your consent, Espressif's ROM images so the ROM's code can be decompiled.
- Peripheral registers named and typed from the chips' SVD files.

The plugin is a native library. Requires a dev build of Binary Ninja for now. The extension manager installs a small Python loader, which asks before downloading the prebuilt library (Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64 or macOS) from this plugin's GitHub release and checks it against SHA-256 hashes shipped with the plugin; restart Binary Ninja to load it. Headless, enable `espressif.loader.autoDownload`.

To uninstall, run Plugins > Espressif > Remove Native Library before removing the plugin.

See https://github.com/jrozner/binja-espressif for details and for building from source.

installinstructions.Darwin: Requires a dev build of Binary Ninja (stable is not supported yet). Install with the extension manager, then accept the prompt to download the native library (or use Plugins > Espressif > Install or Update Native Library; headless, enable espressif.loader.autoDownload) and restart Binary Ninja. To uninstall, run Plugins > Espressif > Remove Native Library before removing the plugin.
